summary: A humorous memo published on April 1. It spoofs SONET by proposing to compress its frames into poetry, calling the method SONET Over Novel English Translation (SONNET). It is informational and not a real protocol.

plainLanguage.summary: This April 1st RFC proposes a fictional way to compress SONET frames by representing them as English sonnets. It describes how the conversion would work and jokes about preserving both network timing and poetic meter.

questions: what is sonnet compression in rfc 1605
subtitle: A comic proposal to represent SONET frames as English sonnets.

tldr.problem: The memo asks, in jest, whether SONET frames could be compressed by translating them into English sonnets.
tldr.mechanism: It proposes matching each SONET payload to a sonnet in a catalog, then translating between the frame and its sonnet at each end.
tldr.outcome: The proposal claims roughly 50% average compression and jokes that timing errors could damage both SONET pointers and poetic meter.

today: RFC 1605 is an Informational joke memo about SONET-to-sonnet translation. It does not specify an Internet standard.

sections.title: The SONNET Proposal
sections.content:
The memo describes SONNET, short for SONET Over Novel English Translation. It proposes translating 810-byte SONET OC-1 frames into approximately 400-byte, fourteen-line decasyllabic English sonnets, claiming roughly 50% average compression.

It says each possible payload pattern would match a sonnet's Cerf catalog number. The memo is written as an April 1st joke.
sections.plainLanguage: The proposal turns each SONET payload into a cataloged sonnet instead of sending the frame as bytes. The claimed size reduction is part of the memo's joke.

sections.title: Frame Conversion and Higher Rates
sections.content:
At the sending end, a SONET OC-1 frame is replaced by its corresponding sonnet; at the receiving end, the sonnet is converted back to SONET. For rates above OC-1, the memo says frames may be interleaved or concatenated, with sonnet representations interleaved or placed one after another in the corresponding way.

The memo labels SONNET compression speeds OCh-#, where “h” indicates half compression and the number represents the uncompressed link speed.
sections.plainLanguage: The sender substitutes a sonnet for a frame, and the receiver looks up the frame again. For higher rates, the proposal carries several sonnet representations in interleaved or concatenated form.

sections.title: Timing in the Translation
sections.content: The RFC says timing must remain consistent within a frame. It jokes that a shift in SONET frames or converted sonnets could harm SONET pointers or, worse, poetic meter.
sections.plainLanguage: The proposal says the translation must preserve timing. Its warning about poetic meter turns a network timing concern into the punch line.

references.text: Cerf, B., "A Catalog of All Published English Sonnets to 1950", Random House, 1953.
